rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up across all seven passes while keeping cost weights low enough that the selector applies them broadly. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain (0.95) since this program is dominated by a few large control-flow-heavy functions (main at ~1KB of text, find, pboard) where flattening destroys reconstructible loop/branch structure; BCF pairs with it to add opaque predicates along the flattened dispatch. SUB and IBR are raised (0.9/0.85) because on a tiny 1.5KB text section arithmetic and branch substitutions contribute disproportionate per-byte resistance at near-zero risk, and round 1 showed the toolchain handles them cleanly. ICALL stays high (0.9) — with only 4 functions, indirect-call wrapping of find/pboard calls meaningfully hampers static call-graph recovery, and its small code-size footprint suits a size-sensitive binary. IGV and SPLIT emphasize DiversityGain (0.9/0.85) to maximize inter-build variance and basic-block fragmentation of the dense main() body. Cost weights are held in the 0.2–0.45 band (highest for FLA/BCF runtime, highest SizeCost for SPLIT) so the optimizer still tolerates overhead on this hot-loop benchmark but avoids compounding size growth, and CorrectnessRisk stays ≤0.15 given the clean round-1 result, leaving headroom to escalate further if this round also passes.
